params.body:
The Gentells app for Android trades the sign-in code at gentells.com itself and keeps the member's access and refresh tokens, so the member stays signed in for up to 30 days instead of a working day. It then needs an Observatory session from that access token, without a new code each time.

## What changes

- **`POST /auth/site/token {accessToken}`** asks gentells.com who the token belongs to (`/api/observatory/me`) and answers with a session, the same as `/auth/site` after a code exchange.
- `siteIdentityOfToken({base, accessToken})` is split out of `fetchSiteIdentity`. `finishSiteLogin(me, send)` is shared by both logins, so the role is decided by one piece of code.
- The route is in the gated-route list and in `guest-writes`' own-credential pattern, like `/auth/site`.
- `docs/design/one-account.md`: a section on the token login.

## Security

gentells.com answers `/api/observatory/me` only for tokens issued to the Observatory's own client (Trendwolves/gentells-site#239). Without that check, any token with the `observatory` scope, including one a member granted to an agent, could open a session here. **Merge gentells-site#239 first.**

## Checked

- `guest-role.test.mjs`, 3 new:
  - the app's own token: no code exchange, gentells.com is asked who it is;
  - a token gentells.com does not answer for is refused, without a user;
  - the token login decides the role like the code login: no Observatory access, no session.
- Full suite 1494/1500. The 6 failures are `report-render`, because the workbench has no `pdftoppm`. Unrelated.
- `tsc` clean.
params.title: POST /auth/site/token: an Observatory session from the app's own gentells.com token
